priorStories.headline: Hundreds of French schools close amid protests
priorStories.body:
French authorities said 400 to 500 high schools were closed or partly closed during nationwide protests over school conditions, with clashes reported in several cities.

A 15-year-old lost a hand and part of his lower arm after picking up a police stun grenade during clashes in Lens, regional newspaper La Voix du Nord reported. A local official did not confirm the precise circumstances of the injury.

priorStories.headline: Three countries activate Saudi defense commitments
priorStories.body:
Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye agreed to begin implementing their collective-defense commitments and make agreed military forces and capabilities available for rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia.

Their joint statement did not specify troop numbers, equipment or a deployment schedule. It said implementation would follow approved arrangements and each country’s laws.

sources.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Pakistan

priorStories.headline: Nigerian military plane crashes with 32 aboard
priorStories.body:
A Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 carrying 25 passengers and seven crew members crashed near Igbokoda in Ondo State. Nigeria’s presidency said personnel aboard had died, and the state’s governor said no survivors had been found.

Search teams had not reached the main wreckage in the surrounding swamp, leaving the death toll and victims’ names unconfirmed. President Bola Tinubu ordered an investigation and three days of national mourning.

priorStories.headline: Optogenetics pioneers win Nobel medicine prize
priorStories.body:
The Nobel Assembly awarded the 2026 medicine prize to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for discoveries involving light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.

Hegemann and Nagel discovered the light-sensitive protein channelrhodopsin. Deisseroth developed its use as a light-controlled switch for nerve cells, giving researchers a way to control selected neural activity.

priorStories.headline: Spain calls November 29 snap election
priorStories.body:
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced plans to dissolve Spain’s parliament and hold a general election on November 29.

Sánchez said he was seeking a renewed mandate after repeated parliamentary deadlock, including lawmakers’ rejection of his government’s housing measures. An extraordinary cabinet meeting will complete the steps needed to call the election.

candidates.summary: Ukrainian drone attacks killed two people and injured nine in the Moscow region overnight, regional Governor Andrei Vorobyov said. The claims and casualty figures were reported from Russian authorities and had not been independently verified.
candidates.title: Moscow region governor reports deaths in Ukrainian drone attacks

candidates.summary: Police briefly detained Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and other lawmakers during a New Delhi march demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over disputed voter-list revisions. Protesters allege the changes favor the governing Bharatiya Janata Party; the Election Commission and government deny wrongdoing.
candidates.title: Indian opposition leaders detained during election protest

candidates.summary: Singapore's Public Service Division referred eight civil servants to police after reviewing property purchases by 191 officers involved in rail planning. The review examined transactions near locations later announced as MRT stations. Coordinating Minister Chan Chun Sing said the referrals warrant further examination but do not establish wrongdoing.
candidates.title: Singapore refers eight civil servants to police after property review

candidates.summary: Kenya confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease linked to the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Kenyan citizen died in a Nairobi hospital after returning from Congo. Authorities began tracing contacts, screening travelers and taking measures intended to prevent further transmission.
candidates.title: Kenya confirms first imported Bundibugyo virus case

sources.name: World Health Organization Regional Office for Africa

candidates.summary: German authorities arrested former foreign intelligence chief August Hanning and former BND official Manfred D. Federal prosecutors allege that Manfred D. supplied Hanning with about 2,000 documents, including classified material, and that Hanning used some intelligence to prepare an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service. The foreign service was not identified, and the allegations have not been adjudicated.
candidates.title: Germany arrests former intelligence chief in espionage investigation

candidates.summary: The European Commission proposed measures intended to prepare the European Union for possible expansion involving countries including Montenegro, Albania, Ukraine and Moldova. The proposals include safeguards aimed at addressing democratic backsliding by future members and limiting political and economic risks for the existing bloc. Adoption would require further action by EU institutions and member governments.
candidates.title: European Commission proposes safeguards for future EU expansion

candidates.summary: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics to Belgian-American physicist Francis Halzen for contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos originating beyond Earth. IceCube uses detectors embedded in Antarctic ice to observe the difficult-to-detect particles.
candidates.title: Francis Halzen wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics

candidates.summary: Defense technology company Anduril said it will invest $3.7 billion to expand production of components for nuclear-powered submarines at the Sparrows Point shipyard near Baltimore. President Donald Trump highlighted the planned investment during remarks at the shipyard. The spending is planned rather than completed.
candidates.title: Anduril plans $3.7 billion submarine-component investment in Maryland

candidates.summary: The National Hurricane Center classified a southwestern Gulf system as Tropical Depression Nine at 2100 UTC, with maximum sustained winds of 35 mph. By 0300 UTC on October 7, it remained a depression moving east at 5 mph. No coastal watches or warnings were in effect, although forecasters advised interests in the Yucatán Peninsula and the northern U.S. Gulf Coast to monitor it.
candidates.title: Tropical Depression Nine forms in southwestern Gulf

sources.name: U.S. National Hurricane Center Public Advisory 1
U.S. National Hurricane Center Forecast Discussion 2

candidates.summary: Russian emergency crews rescued all 23 crew members of the Liberian-flagged tanker Aframax Rio after it caught fire off Russia's Black Sea coast following an attack by an unmanned vessel, Russia's Transport Ministry said. The ministry said the crew members were Indian nationals and no injuries were reported. The account did not identify who carried out the attack.
candidates.title: Russia says 23 rescued from tanker attacked in Black Sea

candidates.summary: The Giants Brigade said it was investigating verified videos showing armored vehicles operated by Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces running over Houthi fighters near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, including people who appeared unarmed. The Houthis alleged war crimes. A brigade spokesperson said some fighters had opened fire after appearing to surrender. Fighting continued in the area Tuesday, and the extent of government territorial gains remained disputed.
candidates.title: Yemeni government brigade investigates videos of fighters being run over

candidates.summary: Attorneys for Tennessee death-row inmate Christa Pike said she had regained consciousness and was speaking while receiving critical hospital care. Pike had remained unconscious after Tennessee's September 30 attempt to execute her by lethal injection failed despite the administration of two doses of pentobarbital. Her lawyers said her prognosis remained unclear and that she faced a long recovery.
candidates.title: Christa Pike regains consciousness after failed Tennessee execution

candidates.summary: A federal judge sentenced Michael Smith of North Carolina to 18 months in prison for a scheme that used hundreds of thousands of computer-generated songs and automated accounts to fraudulently obtain more than $8 million in music-streaming royalties. Smith, who pleaded guilty in March, was also ordered to forfeit about $8.09 million and serve two years of supervised release.
candidates.title: Man sentenced for automated music-streaming royalty fraud

sources.name: U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York

candidates.summary: The European Commission adopted a package intended to prepare the European Union for future expansion. It proposes stronger sectoral safeguards and a new institutional safeguard for future accession treaties, with possible temporary remedies including restrictions on voting rights in serious cases of democratic or rule-of-law backsliding. The package requires further consideration by EU institutions and member states.
candidates.title: European Commission proposes safeguards for future EU expansion

candidates.summary: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics to Francis Halzen for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. IceCube uses sensors embedded in Antarctic ice to detect rare interactions involving neutrinos from energetic processes beyond Earth.
candidates.title: Francis Halzen wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics
